haiku-low.q2: Only in a later release, after the release still using that column or table has been retired.

haiku-low.q4: The public listener is repointed from the old target group to the new one in a single step, with no gradual shift.
haiku-low.q5: Automatic rollback triggers when the 5-minute 5xx rate exceeds 1%, or metrics cannot be read. It repoints the listener to the old colour and stops new instances. Migrations are not reversed; old colour is untouched.

sonnet.q1: Step 4: run once by the deploy job against the shared database, after build/lint and before any new instance starts. The live (old) colour must keep working on the migrated schema (migrations are additive only).
sonnet.q2: Only in a later release, after the release still using that column/table has been retired.
sonnet.q3: All 4 new instances must pass /healthz 3 times in a row (checked every 10s), then the smoke tests via the test listener must pass, all within 10 minutes of the instances starting. Otherwise abort: stop the new instances, leave the public listener untouched, and end the job as failed.
sonnet.q4: In a single step: the public listener is repointed from the old target group to the new one. There is no gradual shift.
sonnet.q5: Triggers: 5xx rate above 1% over a 5-minute window, or the metrics can't be read (checked once a minute from 5 minutes after the switch, within the 15-minute watch). A rollback repoints the public listener back to the old colour (automatic only if it still points at the new colour). It never reverses migrations; the old colour is left running. Automatic rollback also stops the new colour's instances, skips teardown, and ends the job as failed.
sonnet.q6: For 30 minutes after the switch, while the old colour is up. After that (old colour torn down), any rollback is a normal deploy of the previous release. From minute 15 to 30 nothing watches 5xx automatically, so an engineer must notice and start the manual rollback.
sonnet.q7: NOT STATED what state the database is left in (partial changes are not described). The deploy stops, the new release never starts, and the live colour keeps serving. Migrations are never reversed.
sonnet.q8: Read which target group the public listener points at: that colour is live, the other is idle and gets the new release. The LB (the listener) is the only record; if the read fails, the deploy stops.
sonnet.q9: The deploy lock, a CI concurrency group for catalog-web deploys; a later deploy waits in the queue. It's held for the whole deploy, including the 30-minute wait, until teardown. CI releases it when the job ends, even on failure or cancellation.
sonnet.q10: Through the test listener, a non-public LB listener that points only at the idle (new) colour.
sonnet.q11: The deploy job runs them once against the shared database before any new instance starts. The runner skips migrations already recorded as applied; the specific migration tool is not chosen.
sonnet.q12: They are stopped (on automatic rollback the job waits until they are stopped). The idle colour is left empty for the next deploy. If stopping fails, the job still fails and releases the lock, and the next deploy stops any leftover instances in its idle colour before starting (step 5).
